headline: A Micro Center store in California reportedly made a customer show photo ID and sign a no-export pledge before selling a computer with an Nvidia RTX 5090 graphics card.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: the headline reads like a store policy, but the facts rest on one customer's online post at one store, with no comment from Micro Center.
importance_line: Buyers of high-end graphics cards may face extra paperwork and shops may be under pressure to stop smuggling to China, but it is unclear whether this is store-wide, chain-wide or legally required, and how it would work.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, based on a customer's Reddit post, that a Micro Center store in Tustin, California required a buyer of a PC containing an Nvidia RTX 5090 graphics card to sign a form promising not to export it and to give photo ID, the installation location and the intended use. Micro Center has not said why it has started doing this, and Tom's Hardware says it is unclear how the form would stop smuggling, especially as it does not record the card's serial number.
notes: Single-source Reddit claim relayed by Tom's Hardware (Wccftech also reported it). Reader level: written at level five as the brief says; Full_Report rules 5.1 and the Drive phrasing file now list 7/10 for the Full Report (clash already with Rafi), level not changed.
